text:
emily_a: Hey team — on the ACME POC the customer is sending a single POST with ~85MB of extracted text and we hit a 413 from our gateway. Demo is tomorrow, any fast mitigations? :grimacing:

raj_k: Yeah 413 from nginx/gateway. Logs show `client_max_body_size` rejection upstream. We can't change hosted gateway limits for a tenant on short notice.

emily_a: Can we ask them to presign to S3 or split client-side? They're uploading a giant JSON with all pages.

sam_dev: Recommended pattern: upload raw docs to S3 (presigned multipart), then send references or chunked payloads to embeddings endpoint. For embeddings you can chunk into ~5-10k token pieces.

emily_a: Customer asked if there's a streaming or resumable upload option so they don't re-send everything on failure.

raj_k: For hosted customers, easiest is: 1) presign multipart upload to their S3 bucket, 2) do client-side chunking, 3) call embeddings with a list of chunk metadata. If they insist on single request, short-term gzip can help but still hits gateway limits sometimes.

jess_ops: Also flag for enterprise: if they need on-prem or VPC, Private/Dedicated would avoid gateway max body problems entirely. We can accelerate that path for big deals but it has procurement lead time.

emily_a: Can you drop a quick curl example I can send to their engineers?

sam_dev: Sure — example to gzip a chunk file then POST (works if proxy honors Content-Encoding):

```
# gzip json then POST
gzip -c chunks.json > chunks.json.gz
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @chunks.json.gz
```

sam_dev: If that still 413s, split into N requests like `POST /v1/embeddings` for each chunk and then store the vector ids for aggregate search.

raj_k: Quick debug commands we used: check gateway logs for `413` and upstream reason, then tail the app logs for `request body too large`. Example filter: `grep 413 /var/log/nginx/access.log | tail -n 100`

emily_a: They asked about cost/limits — will chunking increase embedding cost?

sam_dev: Yes, cost correlates to tokens processed. If you split, you might duplicate some tokens (overlap) to preserve context, so plan for ~10-20% extra. Recommend compressing and deduping client-side before chunking.

emily_a: They also have a security questionnaire asking if we store uploaded payloads and for how long. Need a one-liner.

jess_ops: One-liner: 'By default Redwood stores transient request payloads only as needed for processing and logs; persistent storage of documents is opt-in and can be configured to use customer-owned S3 for POCs/enterprise.' Add SOC2 mention if they ask.

emily_a: Perfect. Any quick call-to-action I can send to their infra team to unblock now?

raj_k: Ask them to: 1) presign multipart S3 uploads (we can validate presign flow), 2) implement client-side chunking to ~5k token chunks, 3) POST chunks individually and aggregate embedding ids. If they need a demo, we can run a small script to show end-to-end.

emily_a: I'll propose that and offer the gzip fallback. Thanks all :raised_hands:

deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance tonight 02:00-02:30 UTC — no infra changes expected to gateway config.

emily_a: Noted. Ok sending guidance to ACME now.
